sources.title: United States Congress
sources.supportSnippet: The United States Congress is the legislature of the federal government of the United States. It is bicameral, composed of an upper body, the Senate, and a lower body, the House of Representatives. Among its powers are the writing of federal laws, the declaration of war, the levying of taxes, and the appropriation of federal funds.

sources.title: United States Senate
sources.supportSnippet: The Senate is composed of 100 senators, two for each of the 50 states. Senators serve staggered six-year terms and are elected by their state's voters. Each senator represents the entire state. Equal representation in the Senate gives each state the same voice regardless of population.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives
sources.supportSnippet: The House of Representatives is composed of 435 voting members, each of whom represents a congressional district for a two-year term. The number of representatives a state has is based on its population, as determined by the most recent decennial census. The Speaker of the House is the presiding officer, elected by the members.

sources.title: U.S. Civics Test Questions and Answers (M-1778, 2025)
sources.supportSnippet: Q26 — Why do U.S. representatives serve shorter terms than U.S. senators? Acceptable answers: to be more closely connected to the public; to be more responsive to the public; to be more responsible to public concerns. The framers wanted members of the House to be more accountable to public opinion than senators, who serve six-year staggered terms.
